comparable_cases.why_comparable: New restaurant (Bellini) with ABC Type 47 full-bar license at 550 Powell St, 115 m away, same RC-4 zoning district, approved May 2022. Agency referral for ABC license.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a new restaurant with full liquor service on the same block in RC-4 zoning within 5 days, explicitly citing PC Section 209.3 (restaurant principally permitted at ground level). The record notes 'continuation of existing use,' meaning the space was already food/beverage, unlike this dry-cleaner conversion.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: New restaurant (Piranesi) with ABC Type 41 beer-and-wine license at 560 Powell St, 115 m away, same RC-4 zoning district, approved May 2022. Agency referral for ABC license.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved simultaneously with Bellini at 550 Powell (same filing and decision dates), demonstrating Planning's routine approval of restaurant uses with alcohol in RC-4 on this corridor. Both were agency referrals, not discretionary hearings, confirming restaurants are by-right.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant (Key Club) with ABC Type 41 beer-and-wine license transfer at 850 Bush St, 139 m away, same RC-4 zoning district, approved November 2021. Agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Another RC-4 restaurant approval on Bush Street itself, directly comparable to the subject site. Approved in 12 days for an ABC referral. Record notes 'continuation of existing use,' so also a food-to-food succession.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant at 878 Bush St, 172 m away, same RC-4 zoning district, approved July 2021. DPH health permit referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in 19 days. Planning explicitly cited PC Section 209.3 and called it 'continuation of existing use,' showing routine health-permit zoning sign-offs for restaurant uses in RC-4. This was a change-of-ownership referral, not a change of use from a non-food space.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Limited restaurant (Acai R) at 891 Bush St, 171 m away, same RC-4 zoning district, approved November 2020. DPH health permit referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in 13 days. Another RC-4 approval on Bush Street citing PC Section 209.3. Address has had three restaurant approvals in the records (2019, 2020, 2021), showing established food-use pattern on the corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: New ABC Type 41 license for restaurant (Estela's) at 891 Bush St, 171 m away, same RC-4 zoning district, approved September 2019. Agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in 98 days (longer than typical ABC referrals), but still approved without conditions. Confirms RC-4 permits restaurant with beer and wine by right under PC Section 209.3. Same address later saw two more restaurant approvals, showing sustained food-use continuity.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant health permit at 650 Bush St, 169 m away, same RC-4 zoning district, approved May 2018. DPH referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in 7 days with no extracted conditions. Minimal description, but fast approval demonstrates straightforward DPH-to-Planning referrals for restaurant uses in RC-4 when the prior use was also food/beverage.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant (L'Ottavo) with ABC Type 41 at 692 Sutter St, 185 m away, different zoning (C-3-G Downtown General), approved September 2022. Agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved in 2 days. While C-3-G is a different district, it confirms Planning's consistent practice of routine ABC-referral approval for restaurants. Record notes 'continuation of existing use,' so another succession within the same use category.

filing_playbook.action: Contact San Francisco Planning Department zoning counter to confirm formula retail status and floor area requirements.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that you are opening a restaurant at 767 Bush St in RC-4 zoning and need to confirm two things before filing: (1) whether your business qualifies as formula retail under PC Section 178.1 (provide your business name, concept, and any other locations or affiliations), and (2) the floor area threshold for Conditional Use Authorization (PC Section 209.3 states 6,000+ sq ft requires CUA). Ask whether the dry cleaner prior use is a protected service under PC Section 202.12 that would require CUA for conversion. Request written confirmation by email that restaurant use is principally permitted on the ground floor if you are not formula retail and under 6,000 sq ft.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector and file fictitious business name (DBA) with the County Clerk.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register within 30 days of starting business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (plus $4 state fee). You will receive a Business Account Number (BAN) required by every other city department. If your public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, file a fictitious business name statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail ($60–$120), then publish once a week for four weeks in an approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Hire an architect to prepare building permit plans for tenant improvements, kitchen, and change of use.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Engage a San Francisco restaurant architect to prepare stamped plans for the commercial kitchen hood, finishes, equipment layout, ADA upgrades, and any structural or MEP changes. Submit DPH health plan check and DBI building permit applications at the same time so both departments review in parallel. Budget 21–60 days for DPH plan review and 14–120 days for building permit review and inspections.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Certify a food safety manager and enroll employees in food handler card.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At least one owner or employee must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, NRFSP, or 360training) within 60 days of opening; the certificate ($100–$250, valid 5 years) is required at the DPH pre-opening inspection. Every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card ($7–$15, 2-hour online course, valid 3 years) within 30 days of hire.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The day range (14–120 days) and government cost range ($470–$1,000) cover the health permit to operate and building permit with change of use, the two approvals in the entitlement path, measured from application to approval when they are granted. The health permit alone is 14–45 days and $470–$1,000; the building permit is 14–120 days and $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation. These figures assume the zoning status becomes 'allowed' after the two missing inputs (formula retail status and floor area) are confirmed. If either input triggers a Conditional Use Authorization hearing, add 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 for the CUA, and the overall timeline becomes 134–420 days. The cost range does not include construction, architect fees, equipment, or non-government expenses such as workers' compensation insurance premiums. The day count is the time to approval, not to denial or withdrawal; no figures are given for those outcomes because the concept is not proposed for denial.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: 767 Bush St is in the RC-4 (Residential Commercial, High Density) zoning district where a restaurant is principally permitted on the ground floor as a Retail Sales and Service use. No prior permits or applications are on file at this address. The site sits in an extremely dense food and beverage corridor: 33 registered food or drink businesses and 26 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, signaling high undue-concentration risk if alcohol were added later. The immediate block has seen consistent approvals for restaurant uses over the past decade, including two new restaurants with alcohol approved in May 2022 at 550 and 560 Powell (115 m away), both in RC-4 zoning.
